title: reduce streaming token latency: kernel scheduling + KV cache + continuous batching
author: Ethan Clarke
description: Motivation: production workloads saw increased tail latency for streaming token generation when load mixes small and large sequences. This PR reduces per-token latency by adjusting kernel scheduling heuristics, making KV cache lookups non-blocking for hot prefixes, and enabling continuous batching with a dynamic flush cadence tuned to request size distribution. Changes are conservative defaults behind runtime feature flags and include a canary rollout plan. Summary of impact: 95th percentile streaming token latency decreased by ~30% in mixed workload perf runs, median latency improved ~12%, and overall token throughput unchanged. This patchset addresses three correlated causes: (1) kernel scheduling favored large-batch kernels causing token loop stalls for short sequences; (2) synchronous KV-cache eviction/lookups caused brief stalls under backpressure; (3) flush cadence was suboptimal for workloads with interleaved short/long requests. Implementation highlights: introduced a lightweight kernel scheduler that tags requests by expected sequence horizon and prioritizes low-latency kernels for short-horizon streams; converted KV-cache hot-path to use lock-free read path with bounded staleness and offloaded heavy promotable operations to background coalescer; implemented continuous-batching controller that adapts flush cadence using per-model sequence-length histograms and backpressure signals. Feature flags added: runtime.enable_adaptive_scheduler, runtime.kvcache_lock_free_reads, runtime.continuous_batching_adaptive_flush. Testing: unit tests for scheduler heuristics and KV read path, e2e perf harness runs in benchmark-lab, canary rollout to 10% of serving nodes. Rollback: all flags default to off and can be toggled per-deployment; immediate revert PR prepared. Related: ENG-2584 (streaming-tail-latency), ENG-2671 (kv-cache-ops), PRs pr-41256 and pr-42759 for earlier batching work.
